newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp CEO says split of stock possible.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp CEO says split of stock possible.

text.p: KeyCorp Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Gillespie said Thursday the bank holding company could split its stock if the price rises above $60 a share.

"In the past, we split in the $60 neighborhood. Now we're at $54, $55 a share. So a split may be in the offing in the not too distant future," Gillespie said in response to a question at the company's annual meeting here.
Gillespie said during a meeting with reporters that he is comfortable with mid-range earnings estimates of about $1.00 a share for the second quarter.
"I'm comfortable with mid-point of a few pennies on either side of $1.00," he said.
KeyCorp president-elect Henry Meyer III was more specific about the company's expectations and said he expects earnings for the quarter to be between $0.99 to $1.01.
The company is looking at acquisitions in lines of businesses such as equipment leasing or money management, Gillespie said.

KeyCorp also would consider "opportunistic" acquisitions of banking companies to strengthen its position in existing markets, Meyer said. Two markets that KeyCorp might look at are Utah or eastern Colorado.
